compare.title: Comparison
compare.lead: Our composer's drawing beside KAGE's composition of the same IDS: unencoded headwords from the HDIC KRM database, common-use kanji, and characters from earlier review sheets.
compare.dataset: {total} sequences · {krm} unencoded headwords, {joyo} common kanji, {review} review characters · measured {date}
compare.method.label: How these were measured
compare.method.body: The gallery shows {krm} unencoded headwords composed by both sides from the IDS, {joyo} common kanji designed on both sides, and {review} review characters from earlier han-compose sheets. Both drawings were rasterized at 256 px. F1@4 is the harmonic mean of the share of each drawing's ink within 4 px of the other; IoU counts exact ink overlap; layout is the L1 distance between the two 3×3 ink-share grids. For common kanji, 17 have a whole glyph on both sides and three (海, 急, 曜) are composed by this site, so their scores include composition.
compare.method.caveat: KAGE is a reference style, not ground truth. Our typeface is heavier — 1.58× the ink at the median — which lowers IoU and F1; designed glyphs can also differ in variant and stroke design. The layout figure and the drawings show the structural differences.
compare.filter.label: Structure
compare.sort.label: Order
compare.credit: KAGE drawings: zi.tools composes the description from GlyphWiki parts and KAGE renders it.
compare.license: GlyphWiki data is free to use; the KAGE engine is GPL-3.0. The drawings are a snapshot of the run.
compare.operators: Sequences are written in IDS; the boxed symbols are its operators: left-right, above-below, three across, three down and enclosures.
compare.set.label: Set
compare.joyoNote: Most common kanji are designed on both sides; 海, 急 and 曜 are composed by this site, so their scores include composition. The remaining comparisons are type style and variant choice.
compare.reviewNote: Review characters come from earlier han-compose review sheets; some are rare or experimental forms. Both sides draw them from the IDS.

baishi.title: zi.tools IDS Extension
baishi.lead: The zi.tools IDS Extension: the extended IDS of the zi.tools database, as written in （白式）IDS 延展语法导论 of 2026-03-20. Earlier drafts appear as history.
baishi.row.body: A row is the character, a TAB, then its default descriptions. A second TAB may add a group of alternative decompositions.
baishi.operators.body: Seventeen operators as of Unicode 16.0.0, each with a shortcut for the zi.tools composer.
baishi.operators.arity: ⿾ and ⿿ take one component, ⿲ and ⿳ three, the rest two. ⿻ may take an overlap bracket; ⿴ ⿵ ⿶ ⿷ ⿼ and ㇯ an index.
baishi.angles.body: A proposal by 鹏鹏喵 gives ⿿ an angle in brackets. I26 does not adopt it: its grammar gives ⿿ no bracket.
baishi.angles.inference: Both decks draw [90] turned clockwise. Neither says which way an angle turns or what the d in [45d] means.
baishi.variants.body: A variant identifier names a glyph form. Written after a component, without parentheses, it names that component's form. In parentheses at the end of a description, it names the forms the whole description is for; commas join several.
baishi.variants.kinds: I26's grammar lists five kinds: the wildcard, source letters, UCV positions, imaginary UCV and alternate variants. The syntax reads each as a source letter or a lower-case tag.
baishi.chains.body: A chain is written #( … ). Each part is an optional -, one stroke as a character or a letter, then an optional x and a number, or b. A final z closes the chain.
baishi.characters.body: A part may also be a character: the CJK strokes U+31C0–U+31E3, a Han character, ◝◞◟◜, リ 〢 〣 コ or ユ ス.
baishi.curves.body: ◝ ◞ ◟ ◜, or the letters Qa Qb Qc Qd, write curves.
baishi.chainsHistory.first: J22 (2022): letters [HSPwg], a connector between each pair of characters, and curves Q[a-dw-z] with four-digit crossing codes.
baishi.overlap.body: A bracket after ⿻ says how the components cross: a quick slice, a full crossing matrix, or one special case.
baishi.matrix.body: One row per horizontal of 字₂, top to bottom; one cell per vertical of 字₁, left to right. Rows are joined with commas.
baishi.cell.l: A row of only _ that lies left of every vertical.
baishi.cell.r: A row of only _ that lies right of every vertical.
baishi.matrix.simplify: A row of only x or a is left empty, and a row of only . becomes one . When rows between two lines are x and the rest ., the matrix becomes a slice. All x, or a single a, drops the bracket.
baishi.reverseMatrix.body: When 字₂ also has verticals crossing horizontals of 字₁, the roles swap for a second matrix after |.
baishi.overlapHistory: D1 to D3 mark overlaps with l, r, b, c, x, _ and .; D2 and D3 give one mark per stroke of the second component.
baishi.levels.body: The database comes in three files. The notation on this page is that of lv0.
baishi.change.letters: D1 to D3 have twelve case-insensitive letters, among them B, G, X and W. I26 drops B, G, X and a lone W, and case matters: w and b are modifiers.
baishi.change.w: J22 and D1 read w as a bend, so wg is a bending hook. I26 reads Hw as a horizontal with a rounder joint, allowed only after S or P. 乙 #(HPHwg) is the same text under both readings.
baishi.change.t: I26's letter list glosses T as 横折; its figure and its variant letters say 提.
baishi.change.joins: J22 joins strokes with > ^ v and closure codes. D1 replaces them with a minus connector, which I26 calls reversal.
baishi.change.curves: J22 writes curves Q[a-dw-z] with four-digit crossing pairs. D1 writes ◝◞◟◜ and x n. I26 adds Qa to Qd and keeps clockwise arcs only.
baishi.change.crossZero: I26 calls the n of x n a positive integer, but its examples use x0 and its grammar allows 0.
baishi.change.sources: J22 to D3 give five source letters, G H T J K. A4 adds more, with Q for other and G for mainland China and Singapore. I26 makes Q the UCS2003 column and keeps G for one 彐.
baishi.change.dot: In D2 and D3, [.] is a wildcard that fits automatically. In I26, . is a matrix cell: the vertical ends against the horizontal.
baishi.change.commas: D2 and D3 give one comma slot per stroke of the second component. I26 gives one row per horizontal.
baishi.change.slices: I26's slice section counts horizontals from 1 with virtual lines 0 and -0, so 甴 equals [:2]. Its matrix note follows Python slicing from 0, where [:2] would be 由.
baishi.change.rotate: D1 glosses ⿿ as a vertical plus horizontal mirror, and I26 as rotation. The angle proposal is not in I26.
baishi.change.merge: A4 merges 𦡰 ⿰⺼蒪H(T) at lv2; I26 does so at lv1.
baishi.change.ebnf: I26's grammar names rules that are defined under other names, ends Hanzi with a dangling |, and names U+30E4 and U+30E5 in a comment on the range U+31C0–U+31E3.
baishi.doc.note.I26: The current notation. Its EBNF is “仅供参考，并非正式定义” (for reference only, not a formal definition), and it says “部分内容为反向推导” (parts are reverse-engineered). Some rules rest only on Yi Bai's oral explanation.
baishi.doc.note.R102: A proposal; I26 does not take it up.
baishi.doc.note.R101: A proposal; I26 does not take it up.
baishi.doc.note.A4: Unfinished; it stops partway and leaves several kinds unknown.
baishi.doc.note.D3: A beta draft; footer “Copyright © 2024 Losketch, Yi-Bai, 等 | QQ群: 668364339”. Its regular expressions are malformed in places.
baishi.doc.note.D2: A beta draft; the author is named only in the file's metadata.
baishi.doc.note.D1: The author is named only in the file's metadata.
baishi.doc.note.J22: The earliest notation, since replaced. No author is printed.
baishi.heading.dataDifferences: Where the documents and the data differ
baishi.heading.exampleDifferences: Document examples the data writes differently
baishi.data.body: The grammar on this page was checked on every row of yi-bai/ids at {commit} ({date}): {rows} rows of ids_lv0, ids_lv1 and ids_lv2. I26's grammar with two corrections accepts all of them except {rejected} malformed rows.
baishi.correction.C1: The third column is optional. I26 prints it without ?, which rejects every two-column row. Counts are of all rows of lv0, lv1 and lv2, malformed rows included.
baishi.correction.C2: CJK strokes run to U+31E5. I26 stops at U+31E3, and the data has a row for ㇥.
baishi.malformed.slice: A slice after ⿱, which takes no bracket in any document or anywhere else in the data.
baishi.malformed.empty: An empty identifier in the list.
baishi.kind.name: Kind
baishi.datadiff.column: I26's grammar requires the third column; its prose and the README make it optional, and 95,043 lv0 rows have two columns.
baishi.datadiff.strokes: I26 ends the CJK strokes at U+31E3; the data has a row for ㇥ (U+31E5).
baishi.datadiff.readme: The README says every description carries a parenthesised list; 67,790 of 166,921 lv0 descriptions have none.
baishi.datadiff.lv1: I26 says lv1 drops stroke-style component tags. lv1 drops every component tag and also adds or reorders descriptions; 𡕆 is ⿰壴咨(.,T,J) there.
baishi.datadiff.lv2: lv2 also replaces components with tagged ones, as in 与qs, which I26 does not describe.
baishi.datadiff.crossZero: I26 calls the n of x n positive; the data uses x0 11 times.
baishi.datadiff.sourceQ: A4 reads Q as other sources, I26 as the UCS2003 column for Extension B; all 2,904 rows tagged Q are Extension B.
baishi.datadiff.letters: The data uses only I26's stroke letters, in upper case: no B, G or X, and no lone w or g.
baishi.datadiff.unused: Never used in the data: J22's connectors and curve codes, ⿿ angles, ㇯, 〾 and 🔄.
baishi.datadiff.digits: {?1…}, {?2…} and {?3…} occur 5, 14 and 15 times; the documents show only {?…} and {?0…}.
baishi.datadiff.codes: UCV-shaped codes with p, x and y occur, such as p4544, x4523 and y2002; I26 allows them without an example.
baishi.datadiff.otherQ: q tags outside I26's UCV pattern occur, such as q298za2, q0515b2 and q092a.
baishi.datadiff.v: The letter v occurs in (vy) for 望; I26's letter list has no v.
baishi.datadiff.lists: A list may repeat one identifier: (.,.), (J,J), (K,K) and (P,P).
baishi.datadiff.mixed: 36 lv0 rows mix descriptions with and without a list, as 匝 ⿷匚.巾.;⿷匚.帀(q298m2).
baishi.unsettled.zai: What the ⿱[:-1] of 洅 was meant to be.
baishi.unsettled.underscore: Whether overlap strings with _ follow the reading of D2 and D3 or that of I26.
baishi.unsettled.pxy: Whether x4523 and y2002 are UCV codes.
baishi.unsettled.vq: What v in (vy) and long q tags such as q298za2 encode.
baishi.unsettled.lv1: Why lv1 adds descriptions lv0 lacks, as ⿱⺝一 for 且.
baishi.unsettled.order: The order of identifiers in lv1 and lv2 lists.
baishi.formal: The corrected grammar in ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF.
baishi.database.checked: The grammar on this page was checked at the commit of {date}.
baishi.grand.label: Grammar diagram
baishi.kind.order: The patterns below tell the kinds apart, the first match winning.
cheatsheet.title: zi.tools IDS cheatsheet
cheatsheet.composed: Drawn by the workshop's composer from the sequence. Tags are not drawn.
cheatsheet.hint.entries: A row is the character, a TAB, then its entries. A semicolon separates two entries.
cheatsheet.hint.alternative: A second TAB starts a group of alternative decompositions.
cheatsheet.hint.tagDefault: A dot after a component is its default form.
cheatsheet.hint.tagSource: A source letter after a component takes that source's form of it. J is Japan.
cheatsheet.hint.tagParts: One letter for each part of the component: the first two parts of 丰 are unchanged and the third has a 撇 (I26 pp.12–13).
cheatsheet.hint.tagStyle: A tag is an identifier from the component's own row. 子t is the (t) entry of 子, whose 一 takes the shape of 提.
cheatsheet.hint.listSource: A source letter: the entry describes that source's glyph.
cheatsheet.hint.listStyle: A style letter: the variant whose 一 takes the shape of 提.
cheatsheet.hint.listPosition: A position letter, u for up (I26 pp.12–13): 鹿 stands over 木, where the default entry writes ⿸.
cheatsheet.hint.listUcv: q, the three digits of a UCV rule, then the number of the glyph in it: rule 408, glyph 2.
cheatsheet.hint.listAnalogy: qq and a rule number: a variant made by analogy with UCV rule 222 (I26 p.11).
cheatsheet.hint.listMirror: m marks an entry that has a mirrored part.
cheatsheet.hint.listMerged: lv1 drops component tags, so the (.) and (T) entries of lv0 read alike and share one list. The identifier t of lv0 is not kept.
cheatsheet.hint.sourceLetters: G is written for 彐 only, and Q is the UCS2003 column of Extension B (I26 p.8).
cheatsheet.hint.styleLetters: Glosses as printed in I26 pp.12–13.
cheatsheet.hint.positionLetters: Glosses as printed in I26 pp.12–13.
cheatsheet.hint.prefixSame: 土 has the same sequence with no prefix. {士} marks this one as 士.
cheatsheet.hint.prefixDistant: ? marks a source form far from the character's other sources. No document says what the digit means.
cheatsheet.hint.prefixSource: A source letter keeps the prefix to that source.
cheatsheet.hint.chain: Strokes are written in order, each starting where the last one ended.
cheatsheet.hint.reverse: A minus joins the stroke backwards, its start and end swapped.
cheatsheet.hint.cross: x and a number: the stroke crosses the stroke of that number, counted from 0.
cheatsheet.hint.break: b keeps a stroke from merging with the next into one stroke (I26 p.15). The three strokes are drawn where 世 has them.
cheatsheet.hint.closed: A final z closes the chain: the last stroke ends where the first starts.
cheatsheet.hint.letters: A stroke may be spelled in letters. After S or P, Hw turns into 横 with a round joint; g adds a hook.
cheatsheet.hint.slice: The first part's vertical runs between horizontals a and b of the second part. A negative number counts from the bottom, and a missing one lets the vertical stick out.
cheatsheet.hint.matrix: One row for each horizontal of the second part, one cell for each vertical of the first: x crosses, a b c name the segment crossed, . the vertical ends on the horizontal, _ the horizontal ends on the vertical, l and r lie left or right of it (I26 §6.3). D2–D3 read strings with _ another way.
cheatsheet.hint.segment: b: 一 crosses the second vertical segment of ㇉ (I26 pp.20–21).
cheatsheet.hint.reverse2: After the bar, the same description with the roles of the two parts swapped.
cheatsheet.hint.space: [n] puts the second part in enclosed space n of the first, counted from 0. [0] is never written (I26 §6.6).
cheatsheet.hint.workedShi: 凵y in 世 is the (y) entry of 凵, written as three strokes.
cheatsheet.hint.workedMu: A chain inside ⿴ inside ⿻. 𠃊, stroke 1, crosses stroke 0, 𠃌.
cheatsheet.hint.workedYa: Two chains side by side, between two 一.
cheatsheet.hint.workedGui: The J-source form. 乂 stands in enclosed space 4 of the frame.
cheatsheet.hint.unused: ㇯ is for searches on zi.tools (I26 p.26). No document mentions 〾.
cheatsheet.hint.strokeLetters: Each letter is the stroke its own row gives it. Z stands only in ㇘, and W only as Wg.
cheatsheet.hint.spelled: A compound stroke is its simple strokes in order: 𠃍 is H, then S.
cheatsheet.hint.hook: g after a letter adds a hook to the stroke.
cheatsheet.hint.taggable: ユ and ス take a tag, as an ideograph or a stroke does.
cheatsheet.hint.untagged: コ and リ take no tag.
cheatsheet.hint.workedEr: ⿼ around a nested ⿰, the first part tagged. The entry is the J-source form.
cheatsheet.hint.workedWang: Both parts carry a tag: a source letter on 亠, a style letter on 𠃊.
cheatsheet.hint.workedWu: A chain stands as one part under two operators.
cheatsheet.hint.workedHan: A slice, then three levels of nesting. The entry is the J-source form.
cheatsheet.hint.workedChe: A row with an alternative group: two ways to cut one character.
cheatsheet.kind.head: Character
cheatsheet.tip.head: The character this row describes.
cheatsheet.tip.tab: A TAB separates the character, its entries and the alternative group.
cheatsheet.tip.prefix: Braces name the character this entry stands for, where another character has the same sequence.
cheatsheet.tip.katakana: A katakana letter standing as a component.
cheatsheet.tip.tag.source: Source letter {source}: the component in that source's form.
cheatsheet.tip.tag.style: Style and position letters name the entry of the component's own row that carries them.
cheatsheet.tip.tag.other: An identifier from the component's own row.
cheatsheet.tip.stroke: A stroke of the chain, joined where the last one ended.
cheatsheet.tip.break: b keeps this stroke from merging with the next into one stroke.
cheatsheet.tip.list.source: Source letter {source}: the entry describes that source's glyph.
cheatsheet.tip.list.style: Style letters: the variant with those strokes changed.
cheatsheet.tip.list.position: A position letter: a part shifted up, left or right.
cheatsheet.tip.list.ucv: q, the three digits of a UCV rule, then the number of the glyph in it.
cheatsheet.tip.list.analogy: qq and rule numbers: a variant made by analogy with those UCV rules.
cheatsheet.tip.list.mirror: m marks an entry that has a mirrored part.
cheatsheet.tip.list.other: Another identifier that tells the entries of the row apart.
cheatsheet.source.draftsNote: Beta drafts, dated from the files' metadata.
cheatsheet.source.notationBy: designed by 白易, compiled by NightFurySL2001 from originals by -PT_AxH_RV- and Losketch.
cheatsheet.source.notationNote: Partly reverse-engineered; its grammar is marked as reference only.
cheatsheet.help.title: About this sheet
cheatsheet.help.colour: A written part and the strokes it names share a colour, and each colour has its own underline. Pointing at either picks out the pair. A token says what it is when pointed at, tapped, or reached with Tab and the arrow keys.
cheatsheet.help.glyphs: The glyphs are the font's own outlines, Noto Sans CJK JP and Plangothic. A part is the contours of its strokes; nothing is redrawn.
cheatsheet.help.entry: Each sequence is the entry of its row for the form drawn: the (J) entry, or the default where the row has none. A variant the font does not draw alone is drawn inside a character whose entry names it, the rest of that character faint. 𱤻 stands for ⿾止 as I26 gives it (p.2).
cheatsheet.help.open: The documents leave open the digit in {?n…}, the reading of overlap strings with _, and what the long q codes stand for.
cheatsheet.help.subject: The marked piece of a sequence is what its card is about.
cheatsheet.help.composed: A tile with a dashed edge is drawn by the workshop's composer from the sequence, for a form no outline has. Its tags are not drawn.
cheatsheet.help.marks: On a chain's glyph a ring marks where the chain takes up each stroke: a square after a break, a filled ring where the chain closes, and a cross where two strokes cross.
ucv.title: Component variations (UCV)
appendix.notation.babelstone: A numbered part with no code point. Note 6 of the file says where each occurs.
appendix.notation.chise: A glyph of the CHISE character ontology, by its name there. The prefix names the set it comes from.
appendix.notation.zi-tools: Strokes in writing order, each starting where the last ended. A minus writes a stroke backwards and a final z closes the line.
appendix.notation.form: This table’s own number for one form, whatever the sources call it. It reads as a part in any description.
library.title: Component library
history.title: Notation history
atlas.search: Character, cid or a character it appears in
atlas.kind.label: Code point
atlas.help.cid: A component’s identifier, apart from any character. ucs:53E3 is the code point U+53E3, which writes 口; chise:GT-K00059 is a part CHISE names that no code point covers. Two older descriptions may call the same part bsp:22 and chise:GT-K00125; both are aliases of one cid.
atlas.help.usedIn: How many descriptions name the component. A character described two ways counts twice.
atlas.help.appearsIn: The characters those descriptions describe, up to {cap} for each component.
atlas.help.unencoded: A part with no code point, which no font draws. The glyph shown for it is GlyphWiki’s.
atlas.help.built: Built {date} from {descriptions} descriptions under {licence}, the licence of the CHISE rows; the BabelStone rows are public domain.
atlas.help.floor: A part named through a CHISE entity that is still unresolved is not counted, so each count is a floor.
strokes.title: Stroke orders
strokes.error.orders: Digits 1–5, with a space between ways
